brief.headline: Rexford Sells $1.3B in SoCal Industrial Assets as Leasing Rebounds
bullets: Real Estate: Rexford Industrial Realty continued its transformation from Southern California’s biggest industrial buyer into one of its largest sellers during the third quarter after completing $1.3 billion in property sales.
Earnings & AUM: Allocators spent the week voting for hedge funds as a diversifier, and the market spent the week testing whether the vote was earned.
Fed & Rates: Investors should focus not on the rate itself.

Real Estate: A joint venture involving Avery Hall Investments, Bridge Investment Group and Declaration Partners has sealed a $95 million loan to refinance a newly built multifamily property in Brooklyn’s Gowanus neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned.

Investor Outlook: Middle East crude flows have rebounded, but precautionary buying and portfolio hedging are among the factors keeping prices elevated, says Daan Struyven, co-head of Global Commodities Research and head of Oil Research, on the Goldman Sachs Exchanges podcast.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,757.17 (up 0.6% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 19.0, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.96% (down 17 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.31 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.40%, near long-run norms (up 13 bps on the prior reading).
